statement: While a dispute is open on an Account, whoever started it (the Entity holds a record of the dispute it asked for, `starting`, or of the one the peer started, `against`, until the finalize, a lapse or the epoch move ends it), the node signs nothing new on it. It proposes no frame (its queue waits), and every frame its peer proposes is refused with the fault `frozen`, which can pass: the proposer takes the frame back and tries again once its view of J moves, so the payment commits in the epoch that follows or is refused then by the Account's own door. The one predicate that says so, `quiet` (the node's signature is out on a settlement or a C2R, R-COSIGN-FREEZE, or a dispute is open), feeds both the proposing and the rules the Account judges the peer's frames by. A command that takes on value (`pay`, `lock`, `offer`, `fill`) asked on an Account in dispute is refused back to whoever asked, with a `command_refused` notice and the fault `account_disputed`, so it is never queued to be zeroed by the rebase; a lock the paybook forwards into it fails back along the route as a refused entry does. When a dispute finalize moves the epoch on and the node's committed head is above the proof the finalize paid by (its nonce, the chain's stored nonce after the finalize, is below the node's own head: a frame the proof does not hold, committed after it was signed or sealed before the dispute and acked after it), each token is told to the node's owner (`offdelta_rebased`: peer, token, epoch, the committed nonce, the offdelta the node counted and the finalized nonce), so a payment the rebase zeroes is never lost without a word. A head at or below the finalized nonce lost nothing and is told nothing, whatever its offdelta; a settlement or a C2R moving the epoch tells nothing (the chain reverts both while a dispute is open, and a settlement folds the offdelta into ondelta). The offdelta the finalized proof holds is not in the notice: the node that lost something did not open with that proof and holds none of its body; the chain's DisputeFinalized for the nonce says what was paid. A frame of the node's own that was sealed before the dispute is not sent again while the dispute is open, and the ack of it commits nothing: it stays pending and is rebased with the epoch like any pending frame. A finalize settled every clause of its proof, so the holds are dissolved (R-HOLD-DISSOLVE) and a release queued for one is refused with a notice, never applied again in the epoch that follows. A payee behind a dispute cannot resolve in a frame, so the secret reaches the hub that forwarded the lock another way: every hosted Entity hears the chain's `SecretRevealed` as `j_secret` (at the configured depth, R-WATCH-READS-ALL) and the paybook passes the secret up for a lock it forwarded under that hash, on any Account, frozen or not; a resolve in a frame the node refuses as frozen shows its secret the same way, since a secret proves itself by its hash. A release (`resolve`, `cancel`, `expire`, `retract`, `lapse`) and `set_credit` wait in the queue for the new epoch. The proof the dispute rests on therefore stays the newest the node holds, and no frame is committed between the chain's finalize and the Entity hearing of it, because the Entity stays quiet until it hears the epoch move. Not here: a frame the peer sealed before it heard of the dispute and that this node acked before it heard of it (the peer commits it, this node's finalize or counter may not hold it; the notice says what the node counted but not what the chain paid, so the finalize may void it unannounced: owed, a notice for offdelta beyond the finalized proof), the Host telling the Entity the epoch before it signs anything, the exact tokens a finalize pays (zeroing the union only understates, never overstates: owed, the Host reads the Account's holdings after the finalizing block), and the starter that never finalizes (owed, the next PR).
source: coordinator 10-02 11:55 (decision after the re-audit of PR 159)

R-DISPUTE-FREEZE only the Account in dispute stops: the others still propose
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE the epoch moving on, or the dispute being over, ends it and the queue goes out
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a dispute the Host dropped, because its start would revert, ends it too
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a payment, lock, offer and fill asked in a dispute are refused with a notice
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE the same payment on an Account with no dispute is taken
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a release or a credit limit is not refused for the dispute, and nothing is sealed
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE once the dispute is over the payment is taken again
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE both sides' payments are refused with a notice and no frame goes out
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE after the finalize the Account is as the chain left it, without the refused payment
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a frame a peer sealed before it heard of the dispute is refused as frozen
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a finalize by a proof below the committed head tells that node both nonces
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a frame sealed before the start and acked after it is told to the committer
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a finalize by the proof the node holds as its head tells nothing
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE an epoch a settlement or a withdrawal moves tells nothing, a repeat nothing more
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a secret Bob shows on the chain is passed up: the hub claims Alice's lock
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a resolve the hub refuses as frozen still gives it the secret to pass up
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a secret nobody forwarded a lock under, or a wrong one, changes nothing
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a lock forwarded into an Account in dispute is refused and given up upstream
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a revealed secret reads hashlock and revealer from topics, the secret from data
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a revealed secret is a j_secret for every hosted Entity and asks no reading
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE a secret the chain showed reaches the Entity as j_secret, in bytes
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE an ack that arrives in the dispute commits nothing: the frame stays pending
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE the timer does not send the pending frame again while the dispute is open
R-DISPUTE-FREEZE when the dispute lapses the frame is sent again, Bob acks it again and it commits
